title: Regional maintenance triggered circuit saturation and priority-shed
creator: Amrita Kapoor
description: During a planned maintenance window in primary-us-west we observed an unexpected control-plane routing adjustment that caused a 3x increase in fanout to secondary-eu region. The secondary region had lower active capacity and cold KV caches; the increased fanout saturated per-region circuit-breaker budgets and triggered priority-based shedding. Resulting behavior: p95 generation latency spiked, several SLO buckets missed for ~2 hours, and some production customers experienced elevated error rates and degraded responses. This ticket documents the incident timeline, root causes, key findings, and tracked follow-up action items.
root_cause: Control-plane maintenance script rebalanced traffic to a narrower set of egress partitions in primary-us-west which caused sticky-affinity drift. That drift amplified traffic routed to secondary-eu. Secondary-eu's autoscale buffer and reserve capacity were insufficient for the sudden increase and its KV cache warmup path had high cold-cache tails. Circuit-breaker hysteresis and per-priority quotas were too aggressive when facing fanout bursts, causing head-of-line shedding that cascaded into SLO misses. No synthetic probe detected capacity mismatch prior to user-facing impact.
timeline: 2025-11-17T02:05Z - Planned control-plane maintenance started in primary-us-west (operator: infra-maintenance-team).
2025-11-17T02:18Z - We observed small routing shifts; telemetry showed rising fanout to secondary-eu (3x baseline).
2025-11-17T02:22Z - p95 generation latency in production increased from 180ms -> 520ms. Alert: SLO-p95-exceeding-threshold fired.
2025-11-17T02:25Z - Circuit breakers in secondary-eu started entering half-open/closed states for priority-low routes; priority-high remained functional but experienced longer tails.
2025-11-17T02:28Z - Priority-based shedding activated; some requests returned 503 for non-critical routes. Incident declared.
2025-11-17T02:40Z - Mitigation: rollback maintenance reroute and emergency expansion of secondary-eu reserved pool by enabling burst nodes (manual scaling).
2025-11-17T03:10Z - KV cache warmup tasks kicked off; tail latencies slowly improved as hot keys warmed.
2025-11-17T04:15Z - Traffic normalized to baseline and SLOs returned within target. Monitoring continued for 24h for regressions.
findings: Control-plane maintenance changed partitioning policy without validating egress fanout impact.
Secondary-eu had only a thin reserved buffer for burst expansion which was insufficient for 3x transient fanout.
KV cache warmup path has non-linear tail growth for cold-start; warming worker concurrency capped at a conservative default.
Circuit-breaker hysteresis values favor quick open and delayed recovery which amplifies headroom loss under simultaneous traffic spikes.
No pre-failover admission-control or synthetic canary run against secondary region capacity before maintenance rollouts.
impact_summary: ~18% of production requests routed to affected routes experienced latency > target p95; SLO breach lasted ~2 hours and consumed ~4x the expected error budget for the day for the affected service. Several enterprise customers reported degraded throughput for non-critical endpoints and one customer issued a paged support ticket.
action_items: [Owner: Liam O'Connor] Update control-plane maintenance playbook to include a pre-commit synthetic canary that validates per-region admission at 2x expected fanout. ETA: 2025-12-01.
[Owner: Priya Nair] Increase secondary region reserved burst pool and lower autoscale cooldown for emergencies. ETA: 2025-11-30.
[Owner: Hana Martinez] Implement progressive KV cache pre-warm on failover with parallelism tuning and a backoff-safe warmup token bucket. ETA: 2025-12-10.
[Owner: Infra-SRE] Adjust circuit-breaker hysteresis and introduce a graded half-open recovery policy that re-injects small steady traffic rather than full reopen. ETA: 2025-12-05.
[Owner: Amrita Kapoor] Add admission-control gate in smart-routing: block >1.5x fanout to any single region unless explicit capacity check passes. ETA: 2025-12-12.
[Owner: Documentation Team] Update runbook and on-call playbook with step-by-step rollback and expansion procedures for maintenance-induced fanout. ETA: 2025-11-24 (completed).

[Owner: Observability] Create a dashboard showing region-fanout ratio, KV-cache-hit-rate, and circuit-breaker-state with 1m granularity; add an automated escalation if fanout > 2x for >5m. ETA: 2025-11-28 (in prod).
mitigations_taken: Rolled back the maintenance reroute within 15 minutes of alerting which stopped further fanout amplification.
Manually expanded secondary-eu pool and kicked off cache warmers to reduce tail latency.
Engaged on-call SRE and launched incident bridge; customer success notified impacted customers within 35 minutes.
postmortem_decisions: Require a pre-maintenance canary for any control-plane change that affects routing or partitioning.
Adopt a 'region-admission' micro-check in smart-routing to gate sudden fanout increases.
Relax circuit-breaker open thresholds under cross-region maintenance to favor gradual degradation over aggressive shedding for priority-high traffic.
next_steps: Track completion of all action items; weekly sync until all ETAs met.
Schedule a cross-team tabletop exercise simulating primary-region maintenance-induced failover. Owner: Resilience PM. Date: 2025-12-08.
Monitor post-deployment metrics for 30 days after changes.
